ttp-attack-mapping-reliability.rationale: HELD AT 3, but the composition of the 3 is corrected this cycle and a successor must not read 'held' as 'unexamined'. Nothing has touched this issue since cycle 16 (attempts [16]). WHAT MY G2 ON src-0005 CHANGED. Cycle 22's rationale said the primary claim 'rests on three unaffiliated teams (src-0002 CTIBench, src-0005 CyberSOCEval, src-0007 CyberThreat-Eval)'. That count was too generous and I am withdrawing it: src-0005 REPORTS NO ATT&CK-MAPPING METRIC AT ALL. A targeted verbatim search of the full text for 'ATT&CK', 'MITRE', 'TTP', 'technique' and 'tactic' returned only the descriptive phrase 'understanding complex attack chains, and mapping tactics to frameworks like MITRE ATT&CK' -- one aspect among several that its Threat Intelligence Reasoning task is said to exercise -- plus an appendix code listing retaining the keys 'tactic, technique' from a mitre_attcks field. This issue's own open_question[0] already suspected exactly this ('did not report a directly comparable ATT&CK-technique-extraction metric'); it is now SETTLED AT SOURCE rather than suspected. So src-0005 is a directional corroborator on general CTI-reasoning headroom, NOT a third measuring leg. THE SCORE SURVIVES THE CORRECTION BECAUSE IT NEVER DEPENDED ON THAT LEG. Candidate 2 (status supported, evidence [src-0007, src-0002]) carries the level-3 bar on its own: two unaffiliated teams, two corpora, both DIRECTLY measuring ATT&CK technique identification -- src-0002's CTI-ATE best-model F1 ceiling of 0.6388 (GPT-4-turbo) against src-0007's precision/recall of 0.2787/0.2270 (GPT-4o), 0.3480/0.1759 (o3-mini), 0.2387/0.1846 (GPT-4o FT), 0.1771/0.1414 (GPT-4o-mini FT) over expert-annotated production material. Those nine src-0007 figures remain the best-verified numbers in this base (verbatim to four decimals at cycle 15, whole-table re-pull at cycle 21). Two independent sources on the primary candidate is a 3. TWO NEW FACTS ABOUT src-0005 THAT WEAKEN ITS CORROBORATION FURTHER, recorded so nobody restores the old three-leg count. (a) Its benchmarks are MULTI-SELECT MULTIPLE CHOICE -- metric verbatim, 'the share of questions for which the system selects all correct options and only the correct options' -- so its percentages are not commensurable with an F1 over free-form technique extraction. This is the third instance in this base of task-format non-commensurability, after src-0003's classification-over-regex-candidates score (cycle 22) and src-0007's substring matcher (src-0017, cycle 21). (b) Its questions were SYNTHETICALLY GENERATED by Llama 3.2 90B and Llama 4 Maverick and then human-validated, and the paper itself concedes both the format limit ('does not provide a perfect proxy for capabilities') and a contamination risk ('performance bias ... where the model under test is the same, or has similarities with the set of models that were used in synthetic data generation pipelines'). WHAT MY G2 ADDED IN THE OTHER DIRECTION, and it is the first quantitative content this source has contributed in 26 cycles: Threat Intelligence Reasoning overall scores 'range from approximately 43%-53%' against a stated random baseline of about 1.7%, and Malware Analysis 'from approximately 23-34%' against about 0.63%. Both verbatim, both attributed to their sections by a confirming fetch. That puts a number on 'far from saturating' for the first time and mildly strengthens the general-headroom half of candidate 1 -- while leaving the ATT&CK-specific claim exactly where candidate 2 already had it. CARRY-FORWARD [10] IS DISCHARGED, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT IT WAS NEVER ACHIEVABLE BY THIS ROUTE. Fifteen-plus cycles asked for src-0005's per-model scores. The paper publishes NO results table; every per-model number lives inside Figures 8, 9, 12, 13, 14, 15 and 16, which are images. Confirmed by two independent HTML fetches (v1 and v2), both instructed to write CANNOT READ rather than infer, per the cycle-25 rule that a single negative verdict is unreliable. No sentence anywhere pairs a model name with a score. Stop spending budget on this without a new route. WHY STILL NOT 4, unchanged and now in its TWELFTH cycle of being merely listed: open_question[1] wants a human-analyst baseline F1 for ATT&CK technique extraction. Every number in this issue is an absolute score with no human reference point, so 'hard, unsolved sub-task' remains an interpretation rather than a demonstrated comparison. A SECOND UNADDRESSED COUNTERARGUMENT, carried from cycle 22 and still live: src-0017 shows src-0007's released IoC evaluator matches by two-directional SUBSTRING CONTAINMENT, and no cycle has pulled the scoring rule for its ATT&CK task, so part of the 0.82-versus-0.28 within-table spread could be a scoring-leniency artefact. That does not touch the ABSOLUTE finding candidate 2 asserts, so the score does not fall; it does mean the within-table control is weaker than cycles 16 and 19 took it to be. RESIDUAL WEAKNESS, DO NOT LET IT BE STRIPPED: src-0005 is an UNREVIEWED PREPRINT as far as this base can establish -- v1 24 Sep 2025, v2 10 Nov 2025, no venue, no DOI but the arXiv one, no affiliations printed; the CrowdStrike/Meta attribution carried since cycle 1 rests on identifying two senior authors, not on the paper. No open contradiction is filed against this issue, so no G3 adjustment applies.

ioc-extraction-reliability.rationale: HELD AT 2, RE-AFFIRMED NOT RE-LITIGATED. Nothing has touched this issue since cycle 21 (attempts [9, 21]); no source has been added and no candidate has changed status since cycle 22 assessed it. THE RULE THAT DECIDES IT IS UNCHANGED: level 3 requires the PRIMARY candidate to rest on at least two INDEPENDENT sources, and no candidate here meets it. Candidate 1 (LANCE 97.6% overall F1 against the manually-validated 1,791-IoC PRISM benchmark) rests on src-0003 alone. Candidate 2 (vanilla-LLM IoC precision 0.8240 GPT-4o / 0.8503 o3-mini / 0.8846 GPT-4o-FT / 0.6944 GPT-4o-mini-FT over 1,310 expert-annotated IoCs) rests on src-0007 alone. Candidate 4 -- that the METRIC confound cannot account for the src-0003/src-0007 gap -- cites [src-0003, src-0007, src-0017], but src-0017 is the SAME TEAM's artefact release for src-0007, and candidate 4's own text concedes it 'rests on ONE independent measurement plus arithmetic'. Three source ids is not three independent sources. That is the textbook definition of a 2. WHAT THE ISSUE HAS ACHIEVED, recorded so the held score is not misread as no progress: the METRIC confound of ctr-0001 is effectively eliminated (cycle 18's arithmetic that reconciliation by metric artefact alone would demand IoC recall of 0.09-0.15, plus src-0007's own Section 4.3 sentence calling IoC extraction 'relatively robust, although improvements in recall and processing efficiency remain necessary'); and src-0017 shows the omitted recall was a REPORTING choice, since eval_ioc.py computes it in the same function as precision. RESIDUAL WEAKNESSES CARRIED FORWARD UNCHANGED FROM CYCLE 22, DO NOT LET THEM BE STRIPPED. (i) src-0003's 97.6% is a CLASSIFICATION score over a regex-extracted candidate set -- verbatim, 'We assume a total of 1,789 candidate indicators, extracted using IoC Searcher, a state-of-the-art rule-based tool', 'LANCE labeled over 99% of all extracted indicators', and Figure 9's caption '... on IoC Classification' -- so it is not commensurable with src-0007's free-form extraction precision. (ii) src-0003 NEVER STATES ITS MATCHING RULE; a targeted verbatim search found no sentence saying how a predicted indicator is compared with ground truth, so that open question is unresolvable from the sources in this base. (iii) src-0003's stored baseline figures (IoC Searcher + whitelist 76% F1, AlienVault OTX 72%, VirusTotal@1 86%) are FIGURE-IMAGE-ONLY and not text-verifiable; the ordering is textually supported but the numbers must be cited as figure-derived. CONTEXT ADDED THIS CYCLE FROM ELSEWHERE, not enough to move anything: my G2 on src-0005 found a THIRD instance of a source's headline numbers being locked in unreadable figures, and a THIRD instance of task-format non-commensurability across this base. Both patterns were first identified on this issue. That raises the prior that ctr-0001's SYSTEM confound is the right explanation, but a raised prior is not evidence and no cycle has demonstrated it. G3 GATE ARITHMETIC, STATED SEPARATELY SO IT IS AUDITABLE, and this is the SEVENTEENTH cycle the specification divergence has stayed latent. Merit score on the evidence = 2. ctr-0001 (opened cycle 9, resolved_cycle null) is filed against this issue, so the gate applies. I applied the CEILING reading verified at source this cycle: scripts/validate_state.py lines 144-156 error only when an issue with an open contradiction scores GREATER THAN scale_max - g3_contradiction_demotion = 3. Merit 2 is under the ceiling, so THE CEILING DID NOT BIND and the two readings still have not been forced apart. Under the SUBTRACTION reading that prompts/t4_assess.md step 3 and config.yml line 35 both state, this issue would read 0 -- stamping an issue with four candidate_resolutions with the rubric label 'no candidate resolutions' and handing the weakest-link selector a fabricated bottom, silently, because subtraction never trips the validator. Cycle 16 ruled for the ceiling; prompts/, config.yml and scripts/ are outside this agent's output surface, so this awaits a human (carry-forward [4], sixteenth cycle). WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY MOVE THIS SCORE: a second independent measurement of report-level IoC extraction, or a head-to-head. Of ctr-0001's three confounds METRIC is eliminated, SYSTEM has a paper-stated anchor in task format, and CORPUS is completely untouched and is now the largest gap. ctr-0001 stays open and a T4 has no standing to close it.

consistency-calibration-as-failure-mode.rationale: HELD AT 2, AND THIS IS THE CYCLE'S HARDEST CALL, SO THE REASONING IS GIVEN IN FULL AND A SUCCESSOR SHOULD AUDIT IT HARDEST. Cycle 25's T3 (attempts now [3, 15, 16, 25]) broke a blocker that had held since cycle 3, and the cycle-26 queue entry was explicit that both 2 and 3 are defensible. I take the 2, under step 5's instruction to give the lower score when torn. NAMING THE SPLIT, WHICH IS WHAT THE HANDOFF REQUIRED OF ME. This issue's title asks TWO things: are CTI outputs consistent across repeated queries, AND are they well-calibrated in stated confidence. The evidence is now ASYMMETRIC across those two conjuncts. The CONSISTENCY leg on CTI is genuinely two-source: candidate 5 (added and promoted cycle 25, evidence [src-0001, src-0018]) pairs src-0001 (Mezzi/Massacci/Tuma, ARES 2025, 350 real reports, 3 models, ten re-prompts per input at temperature=0 with a fixed seed -- so the measured spread is residual non-determinism under MAXIMAL determinism settings -- max CI width 0.02 extraction against 0.06 generation) with src-0018 (Milenkoski and Cirstea, SentinelLabs, 9 March 2026, IOC/hash/playbook extraction from narrative threat reports, 343 atomic IOCs and 1859 labeled contextual-attribute instances, five current-generation models, repeated identical runs, two purpose-built decision-consistency metrics). Independence is clean -- no shared author, academia against industry lab, disjoint model sets a generation apart, no citation -- and it clears the cycle-16 scope ruling on that ruling's own terms rather than overturning it, because src-0018 is CTI proper. The CALIBRATION leg on CTI is still SINGLE-SOURCE: src-0001 alone, gpt4o only, nine table rows, and cycle 25's three targeted searches found no other source measuring ECE/Brier on a CTI task (CTIArena, arXiv 2510.11974, was fetched and positively KILLED as a candidate -- it measures neither repeat-query consistency nor calibration). WHY THAT SPLIT RESOLVES TO 2 AND NOT 3. Level 3 asks whether the PRIMARY candidate has two independent sources. The candidate that answers BOTH halves of the title question is candidate 2 (evidence [src-0001]) -- single-source, and additionally the carrier of the gloss that ctr-0003 now disputes. The candidate with two sources, candidate 5, answers only the CONSISTENCY conjunct and says so in terms. Declaring the half-answer primary in order to reach a 3 would be scoring the issue for a question it does not ask. Two further discounts point the same way. (a) src-0018 SUPPLIES NO MAGNITUDE: all four of its quantitative artefacts -- the 'LLM decision consistency' table, the 'Abstention error rates' chart, and the 'Selective IOC extraction performance' and 'Value assignment performance' charts -- are images this agent cannot read, verified by two fetches instructed to say so rather than infer. Its corroboration is of DIRECTION AND EXISTENCE only, and nothing may be compared against src-0001's CI widths. (b) src-0018's abstention metrics (FDR/FNR over an explicit None class) are a RESTRAINT construct, not ECE/Brier, and must never be pooled with proper-scoring calibration -- the same non-pooling rule already recorded for src-0015. WHAT ctr-0003 DOES AND DOES NOT DO. Opened cycle 25 against this issue. src-0001's Table 6 was pulled whole for the first time (caption verbatim 'ECE and BS with gpt4o for information generation and extraction', nine rows where the base had stored five). Every stored cell is EXACT, but the stored gloss 'calibration markedly worse for information-generation than information-extraction' does NOT hold row-wise at zero-shot: generation goals 0.13, CVE 0.15 and country 0.19 all beat extraction campaign 0.25 and CVE 0.28, and the gloss's own worked example (CVE generation 0.15) beats its extraction counterpart (0.28). What survives is a mean gap that is small at zero-shot (0.278 against 0.205) and large only after fine-tuning (0.538 against 0.295), driven by two fine-tuned generation rows -- and all four means are DERIVED BY THIS AGENT, not printed. So the single-source calibration leg is not merely thin, its headline framing is the thing under dispute. A T4 has no standing to repair it; per the entry's own resolution path that is a T3's job. THE FOUR CYCLE-15 SOURCES STILL CONTRIBUTE NOTHING TO THE SCORE, and cycle 16's scope ruling is endorsed rather than re-litigated: src-0013, src-0014, src-0015 and src-0016 each measure a security-ADJACENT task (secure code generation, CVE-code vulnerability detection, JavaScript SAST review, simulated incident response), none measures IoC extraction, TTP mapping, attribution or report drafting, and none tests a model from src-0001's, src-0002's or src-0005's lists. Promoting on them would assert the very cross-domain generalisation this issue treats as open. They establish that the MECHANISM is not one team's artefact, which is real and is held as context. Note also that if candidate 3 were ever promoted, one of its legs (src-0016) carries a known quotation defect found at cycle 21 -- a stored 'verbatim' quotation that splices a real sentence to a table cell. ALL SIX open_questions remain open; two were sharpened at cycle 25 and one (the gpt4o-specificity question) was answered in the negative in the sense that the source CANNOT settle it, because it reports no ECE or Brier figure for gemini-1.5-pro-latest or mistral-large-2 anywhere. G3: ctr-0003 is open against this issue, so the gate applies. Merit 2; CEILING reading applied per cycle 16 and verified at scripts/validate_state.py lines 144-156, ceiling = 5 - 2 = 3; merit is under the ceiling so THE CEILING DID NOT BIND. Under the subtraction reading in prompts/t4_assess.md step 3 this would read 0, which is why the divergence matters (carry-forward [4]). WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS A 3, concretely: either recover magnitudes from src-0018's four images by some route this agent has not found, or have a T3 execute ctr-0003's resolution path -- rewrite candidates 1 and 2 to the mean-and-fine-tuning version, close the entry, and designate a primary candidate that actually covers both conjuncts. CARRY-FORWARD [37] IS ENDORSED AND STRENGTHENED BY THIS ASSESSMENT: the two conjuncts are now legs of visibly different strength, and only a T2 can split them. Split, the consistency child would plausibly score 3 and the calibration child 2; unsplit, the title binds them and the weaker leg governs.

attribution-confident-wrong-gap.rationale: LOWERED 3 -> 2. THIS IS THE ONLY SCORE THAT MOVES THIS CYCLE. It moves because ctr-0002 (opened cycle 23, resolved_cycle null) destroyed the specific evidential move that made this issue's benchmark leg count, and no cycle has yet repaired it. Cycle 23 was a T5 and recorded in the contradiction entry itself that 'a T4 may then rescore'; this is that rescore. WHAT THE 3 RESTED ON, in cycle 22's words: 'an academic benchmark plus investigative reporting on a production incident', where the benchmark contribution was src-0002's CTI-TAA showing 'every one of five tested models' plausible-sounding attribution rate exceeds its correct rate -- GPT-4-turbo 86% plausible against 52% correct, Gemini-1.5 74% against 38%'. WHAT ctr-0002 ESTABLISHED, verbatim from the source's Section 4.2: 'we compute two types of accuracy: Correct Accuracy, which is the fraction of correct answers, and Plausible Accuracy, which is the fraction of correct and plausible answers combined.' The two columns are NESTED. Plausible CONTAINS Correct, so 'plausible exceeds correct' is TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION for every model and every dataset and cannot be evidence of anything. And the paper's plausible bucket is explicitly NOT its hallucination bucket -- plausible is scoped to UNDERDETERMINED INPUT answered with a related actor, while 'misjudgment, hallucination, or spurious correlation' is a separate third category. The string 'plausible-sounding' does not occur in the paper although the state presents it in scare quotes, and no sentence in the paper interprets the gap. All 25 stored numeric cells re-verified EXACTLY against Table 1 across two independent fetches; this is an interpretation defect, not a numerical one. WHY THAT COSTS A POINT RATHER THAN NOTHING. This issue's distinctive content is the CONFIDENT half -- that CTI models emit wrong attributions that read as authoritative. Strip the by-construction gap and count what is left for that specific claim: src-0004 is ONE production incident (ENISA/APT29 misattribution) whose AI-causation rests entirely on Der Spiegel via Heise, with spiegel.de unreachable to this agent, so it is reported-not-primary and n=1; and src-0007's Table 4 rubric block (GPT-4o 1.547 Relevance / 1.528 Accuracy / 1.140 Attribution against 3.686 / 3.458 / 3.612 on Root Cause in the same table) measures attribution QUALITY, not expressed confidence, so it evidences wrongness without evidencing confidence. That leaves the issue's central claim with one quantified-but-off-target source and one anecdote: '>=1 candidate with single-source support', which is the rubric's definition of a 2. WHAT I AM NOT DOING, and it matters for how a successor reads this. I am NOT asserting the issue is empty. ctr-0002's reading (a) is live and may well be right: the paper's incorrect bucket IS hallucination-inclusive by its own definition and equals 100 minus Plausible Accuracy -- GPT-4-turbo 14%, GPT-3.5-turbo 38%, Gemini-1.5 26%, LLAMA3-70B 20%, LLAMA3-8B 64% -- and a 14-64% outright misattribution rate on 50 real reports is a real finding. But those five values are DERIVED BY SUBTRACTION AND NOT PRINTED IN THE PAPER, and no candidate_resolution in the graph asserts them; the graph still says what ctr-0002 refuted. I score the state as it stands, not as it could be repaired. Per carry-forward [36] the repair -- rewriting the primary candidate, choosing between readings (a) and (b), and checking src-0002's other two key_claims for similar unstated gloss -- is a T3's job and a T4 has no standing to do it. IF a T3 adopts reading (a) and rewrites the candidate to cite the derived incorrect-bucket rates with their derivation stated, this issue returns to 3 immediately and I would expect it to. That makes the demotion a POINTER TO NEEDED WORK, which is what the weakest-link selector is for, rather than a verdict that the issue is weak. TWO ITEMS CARRIED UNCHANGED. (1) open_question[2] -- whether src-0004's naming-convention hallucination is the same phenomenon as src-0002's quantified gap or a distinct citation/naming-fabrication sub-type -- is now in its TENTH cycle merely articulated, and ctr-0002 makes it sharper rather than moot: if the ENISA error is a citation-fabrication sub-type then that leg belongs to institutional-incident-real-world-impact and this issue is closer to single-source than even this 2 suggests. (2) src-0007's GPT-4o (FT) column reads 3.964 / 3.655 / 2.967 against o3-mini's 3.964 / 3.656 / 2.968, tracking to within 0.001 on all six rubric rows across two independent pulls -- as-printed, not a fetch artefact, cause unknown, and any claim resting on that column must say the column is suspect. The rubric's ABSOLUTE level is also uninterpretable (1.140/5 normalises to 0.228 or 0.035 depending on x/5 versus (x-1)/4, a normalisation the paper never states), so only within-table contrasts may be cited. G3: ctr-0002 is open against this issue, so the gate applies. Merit 2; CEILING reading applied (scripts/validate_state.py lines 144-156, ceiling = 5 - 2 = 3); merit is under the ceiling so THE CEILING DID NOT BIND -- the demotion is a merit judgement about the evidence, NOT a gate artefact, and a successor must not restore a 3 by arguing the gate was misapplied. Under the subtraction reading this would read 0.

task-dependent-reliability-framing.rationale: HELD AT 3, on cycle 22's reasoning, which I re-checked rather than took on trust. Nothing has touched this issue since cycle 16 (attempts [6, 16]). THE LEVEL-3 BAR IS COMFORTABLY CLEARED: two supported candidates rest on seven distinct sources from at least five unaffiliated teams (candidate 1 [src-0001, src-0002, src-0003, src-0005, src-0006], candidate 2 [src-0007, src-0013]), and the qualitative claim that measured CTI reliability varies sharply by sub-task is not in doubt. WHY IT IS NOT BACK TO 4. Cycle 22 lowered it from 4 for a counterargument the issue does not state anywhere: a within-study design holds team, corpus, models and harness constant but DOES NOT HOLD THE SCORING RULE CONSTANT, and cross-sub-task spreads are task-difficulty facts only if the sub-tasks are scored comparably. That objection is not merely undischarged, it is now supported by a THIRD instance. Cycle 21 found src-0007's IoC evaluator matches by two-directional substring containment with no ATT&CK-task rule ever pulled (src-0017). Cycle 22 found src-0003's 97.6% is a classification score over a regex-extracted candidate set. My G2 this cycle adds src-0005: its benchmarks are MULTI-SELECT MULTIPLE CHOICE, metric verbatim 'the share of questions for which the system selects all correct options and only the correct options', with LLM-generated questions and an author-acknowledged contamination risk -- so src-0005's leg of candidate 1 compares an all-or-nothing multiple-choice accuracy with F1s and precision/recalls over free-form output. Three of the eight sources in this issue's evidence list are now known to score their tasks in mutually non-comparable ways, and the issue still does not mention the problem. An issue cannot be credited with addressing an objection it has not noticed. TWO NEW DATA POINTS FROM MY G2, PULLING IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, both recorded rather than netted off. FOR the issue: src-0005 now supplies its first numbers in 26 cycles, and they are a within-study cross-task spread -- Threat Intelligence Reasoning 'range from approximately 43%-53%' against Malware Analysis 'from approximately 23-34%', same paper, same model set, same multiple-choice format and same all-or-nothing metric. That is a roughly twenty-point gap between two CTI-relevant task types with the scoring rule genuinely held constant, which is the cleanest form of the evidence this issue wants. AGAINST: the two benchmarks differ in more than sub-task -- different corpora (detonation reports against threat reports), different question-generation pipelines, and different random baselines (0.63% against 1.7%, so the two are not even equally hard to hit by chance) -- so it is not a controlled contrast and I am not entering it as one. It is suggestive, and a T3 wanting to use it must state those confounds. NOT ALL LEGS ARE AFFECTED BY THE SCORING-RULE OBJECTION, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A 3 AND NOT A 2: src-0007's rubric contrast (Threat Actor 1.140 against Root Cause 3.612) is measured on ONE instrument and is immune to it, and src-0006's nine rows are all F1 on one corpus and model set. The claim remains supported; it is the ROBUSTNESS that fails. ONE NEW QUALIFICATION ON A LEG, from ctr-0003 (opened cycle 25 against a different issue): src-0001's extraction-versus-generation split is used here as a calibration data point, and the CALIBRATION half of that split no longer holds row-wise at zero-shot -- three generation rows are better calibrated than two extraction rows. The CONSISTENCY half (CI widths 0.02 against 0.06) is re-verified and stands. A cycle citing src-0001 on this issue must keep the two halves apart and must not carry the 'markedly worse' framing. This does not lower the score because src-0001 is one of five sources on candidate 1 and the consistency half survives intact. WHAT RESTORES 4, unchanged and concrete: pull src-0007's per-task evaluation protocols from the src-0017 artefact (the IoC evaluator is read; the TTP and rubric scorers are not) and src-0006's per-task scoring definitions, then STATE AND ANSWER the objection in the issue text. If the scoring rules turn out comparable, cycle 19's argument stands as written and the 4 is correct. WHAT IS NOT A COUNTERARGUMENT, carried from cycles 19 and 22 because the reasoning is still right: cycle 18's derivation that src-0006's mean between-MODEL range within a task (0.272) nearly equals the mean between-TASK range within a model (0.263) does not undercut this issue -- a mean between-task range of 0.263 within a single model, running to 0.404 for LL70, CONFIRMS that reliability varies by sub-task. What it undercuts is sub-task as the PRIVILEGED explanatory variable, which lives in the child issue. RESIDUAL WEAKNESSES CARRIED, DO NOT LET THEM BE STRIPPED: src-0013's leg of candidate 2 measures secure code generation, not CTI, and defers to the cycle-16 scope ruling; candidate 1's prose still contains superseded ordinal-axis language that the cycle-16 split moved out of this issue, and a future T2 or T3 should annotate rather than delete it; src-0003's stored baseline figures (76/72/86) are figure-image-only and must not be cited as reported values; and src-0005 is an unreviewed preprint whose per-model numbers are permanently unreadable by this agent. Three open_questions remain, so 5 was never in view. No open contradiction is filed against this issue, so no G3 adjustment applies.

extraction-vs-reasoning-ordinal-axis.rationale: HELD AT 3. Nothing has touched this issue since cycle 18 (attempts [17, 18]). SCORED ON EVIDENTIAL STATE, NOT ON THE POLARITY OF THE ANSWER: the title question is answered in the NEGATIVE -- the proposed ordinal ranking is not supported -- and a supported negative answer is a supported resolution, since the rubric is definitional about whether a supported resolution exists rather than about what it concludes. The primary candidate is supported by two independent sources from unaffiliated teams on different corpora with disjoint model sets, by two distinct routes. Route 1, src-0006's Table 2 restricted to its nine F1 rows: Contextualization-stage mean 0.636 against Attribution-stage mean 0.602, a gap of 0.034 that is in the predicted direction but is roughly one eighth of the 0.272 mean between-model spread on a single task, and the best-performing task in the whole subset is TTP Extraction at 0.673, an Attribution-stage task -- so the ordering is not merely weak, it is locally INVERTED at its strongest predicted point. Route 2, src-0007's Table 4, the source that appears to support the ordering, reverses its own middle-to-third rung between two models of the same family under both defensible normalisations. WHY THE ACCUMULATING NON-COMMENSURABILITY FINDINGS DO NOT LOWER THIS SCORE, EVEN THOUGH THEY LOWERED THE PARENT ISSUE. src-0017's substring-containment finding (cycle 21), src-0003's classification-score finding (cycle 22) and my src-0005 multiple-choice finding (this cycle) all undermine confidence that cross-sub-task numbers are commensurable. For the PARENT that is adverse, because the parent's supported claim asserts a real cross-sub-task difference. Here it is neutral-to-favourable, because this issue's supported claim is EVIDENTIAL and NEGATIVE: that the available commensurable measurement does not support the proposed ordering. Less commensurability means less evidence for the ordering. I checked the reverse reading -- that route 1 is weakened because its own 'commensurable measurement' may not be commensurable -- and the outcome is unchanged: under that reading no commensurable measurement supporting the ordering exists either, so the negative claim survives both ways. SAME TREATMENT FOR ctr-0003, which is new since this issue was last scored. It disputes src-0001's extraction-versus-generation CALIBRATION gradient, one of the apparent supports for an extraction-beats-generation ordering. Removing an apparent support for the ordering does not weaken a claim that the ordering is unsupported. Note src-0001 is not in this issue's evidence list, so nothing is recalculated; the entry is noted because ctr-0003's own text names this issue as a consumer of that split. WHY 3 AND NOT 4. Level 4 needs counterarguments addressed and the candidate states four material caveats of which only one is addressed. (a) src-0006 reports no confidence intervals, no seeds and no repeat runs, so the headline 0.034 carries NO uncertainty estimate -- stated, not addressed, and not addressable from any source in this base. (b) Four of the nine rows are strictly monotone decreasing across all eight general-purpose model columns in exactly the printed order; this one IS addressed, by a robustness check dropping all four, leaving 0.641 against 0.592, gap 0.049, same direction, same best task. (c) THE DECISIVE ONE: the fourth rung of the proposed ordering, open-ended GENERATION, is not represented in the commensurable subset at all, so the candidate refutes only part of a four-rung ordering and is SILENT on one quarter of the ordering named in this issue's own title. (d) per-task scoring rules within src-0006's nine F1 rows have never been pulled, so 'all in F1' establishes that the statistic is constant, not that the matching rules behind it are. Seven open_questions remain, two of them fundamental. WHY NOT 2, since step 5 says take the lower when torn, and I want to record that I considered it seriously for the second cycle running. The honest case for 2 is that route 2 is DEFEATING rather than CONFIRMING evidence, which would leave src-0006 alone carrying the claim and make it single-source. I resolve to 3 on the same ground cycles 19 and 22 did: for a claim whose content is explicitly evidential, showing that the strongest apparent supporting source self-destructs on its own printed table is direct evidence for that claim, and the local inversion (TTP Extraction at 0.673 beating every Contextualization task) is a qualitative fact about a printed table that does not depend on the missing uncertainty estimate. I am not torn enough to move it, and nothing this cycle bears on the question either way. A successor that takes the other view should drop it to 2 and say so plainly. THE THIRD CANDIDATE IS CORRECTLY 'proposed' AND CONTRIBUTES NOTHING: model identity as the replacement explanatory variable, resting on the between-model 0.272 against between-task 0.263 near-equality, which cycle 18 itself objects to on three grounds (ranges are not variance components and are outlier-sensitive, the cross-source TTP comparison behind its corpus-identity limb is uncontrolled in at least four ways at once, and both figures come from one study's table). No open contradiction is filed against this issue, so no G3 adjustment applies.

institutional-incident-real-world-impact.rationale: HELD AT 3. Nothing has touched this issue since cycle 12 (attempts [12]); no source has been added and no candidate has changed status, so this is a re-affirmation and the cycle-13 reasoning that raised it from 2 to 3 stands unamended. THE EXISTENCE CLAIM is carried by candidate 2 with evidence [src-0009, src-0010, src-0004]: ENISA's OWN publication pages carrying verbatim revision notices against publication dates of 1 October 2025 and 6 November 2025, both revised 09 January 2026, corroborating report count, dates, defect type and correction date independently of the Der Spiegel/Heise chain that was previously the entire basis. And by candidate 3 with evidence [src-0012, src-0004]: a second named incident at a different institution type (EY Canada, 16 of 27 references hallucinated per GPTZero, report withdrawn), discovered by the identical route of an outside party clicking through footnotes. Two incidents at two institutions via two mutually independent investigations, plus the affected institution's own correction record, clears the level-3 bar. NOT RAISED TO 4, and the two reasons are unchanged and both structural. (a) THE BASE RATE IS UNMEASURED AND IS BLOCKED BY SCOPE, NOT BY EVIDENCE VOLUME. Two named incidents are two data points, not a rate, and open_question[0] asks for a rate across CTI publishers. src-0011 (GhostCite) is not that rate and its candidate is correctly 'proposed': it audits peer-reviewed conference papers, which have reviewers where CTI reports have none; it defines a ghost citation as one absent from any major academic database, largely inapplicable to CTI footnotes which are news and vendor URLs; it reports per-PAPER rates (1.01% of Security-venue papers containing at least one invalid citation) not comparable with src-0004's per-FOOTNOTE 26/492; and its own authors call it a conservative lower bound. Treating a second anecdote plus an adjacent-population audit as a resolved base rate remains the most likely error available on this issue and it is not being made. Note also that src-0011 contradicts itself in prose versus table (body text says NeurIPS exhibits 'the highest absolute count (391 papers)' while Table 3 gives 391 invalid citations across 308 papers), so any cycle quoting its counts must take them from Table 3's columns. (b) THE AI-CAUSATION LEG IS THE WEAKEST PART AND IT IS THE PART THE TOPIC IS ABOUT. For ENISA, AI attribution rests entirely on Der Spiegel via Heise (src-0004); ENISA's own pages assign no cause at all, spiegel.de is unreachable to this agent, and every outlet repeating the 26-of-492 figure cites Der Spiegel, which is repetition rather than corroboration. For EY the 72% AI figure is the output of GPTZero's own commercial AI-detection product, so the load-bearing element there is the manually-checkable citation count. What is robustly established is that FABRICATED CITATIONS reached production at two named institutions; that AI CAUSED them is well-supported for EY and reported-but-not-primary for ENISA. A PERMANENT LIMIT RATHER THAN A PENDING ITEM: the two ENISA v1.2 PDFs cannot be opened by this agent at all (no PDF text extraction exists on this runner), so 'ENISA never disclosed the AI use' is established at landing-page level and is UNVERIFIABLE at document level here. That leg cannot strengthen and no further budget should be spent on it. Three of five open_questions remain wholly or mostly open, and candidate 4 itself honestly concludes there is no single institutional response pattern to report -- an accurate non-answer on n=2, not a resolution. ONE CROSS-ISSUE NOTE ADDED THIS CYCLE, which could grow this issue rather than shrink it: I lowered attribution-confident-wrong-gap to 2 partly because ctr-0002 removed its quantified leg, and that issue's open_question[2] asks whether src-0004's ENISA error is a distinct citation/naming-FABRICATION sub-type rather than the same phenomenon as a benchmark attribution gap. If a future T2 or T3 answers that in the affirmative, src-0004's fabrication content belongs primarily HERE, and this issue's candidate 2 would gain rather than lose. Nobody has argued it either way in ten cycles. NO G3 ADJUSTMENT: no contradiction is filed against this issue, and cycle 12's reasoning for not opening one over ENISA's silence is endorsed -- the revision notices assign no cause at all, and silence is not a competing claim, so G3's 'two supported claims in conflict' is not met. That is the same test I applied this cycle in declining to open a contradiction over src-0005's unrecorded task format, and the consistency is deliberate. Best available route to a 4 remains GPTZero, which runs an automated pipeline over the right population and publishes findings one report at a time -- the only lead any cycle has found that could produce a rate rather than another anecdote.

automated-triage-under-refusal.rationale: HELD AT 2. This issue still has attempts [] -- it is the only issue in the graph never worked on -- and nothing has touched it since cycle 21's Table 4 pull gave it evidence as a by-product. THE FORMAL READING WOULD GIVE 3 AND IT IS STILL WRONG. The single candidate_resolution is at status 'supported' with evidence [src-0007, src-0015], which on a mechanical count is two independent sources on the primary candidate. The state itself forbids that count: src-0015's own index entry records it as THE WEAKEST-PROVENANCE SOURCE IN THIS BASE and says in terms that it must not be the sole support for any candidate_resolution -- single-author preprint filed cs.AI with no stated venue, peer review or affiliation; n = 40 synthetic RL-seed episodes per model from a 60-seed pool with no confidence intervals, so only the GPT-5.2-versus-Sonnet-4.5 contrast is robust and the middle two models' ordering is unresolved. The candidate itself agrees, stating that the claim RESTS on src-0007 and that src-0015 'is worth little as independent quantification'. Two sources of very unequal quality must not read as two independent confirmations, so what this issue has is one load-bearing source plus a directional corroborator: a 2 by the rubric's definition of partial evidencing. WHAT IS SOLID, and it is table-verified rather than summary-derived since cycle 21: src-0007's triage precision/recall asymmetry holds as stated -- across both triage tasks and all four models, precision (Accepted) spans 0.2717-0.3982 and recall (Accepted) spans 0.9091-1.0000. Fine-tuning does not fix the asymmetry and on the Article task WORSENS precision (GPT-4o 0.3037 -> GPT-4o FT 0.2717 with recall unchanged at 0.9798-1.0000), the same direction as src-0001's fine-tuning finding and cycle 16's ATT&CK finding. THE DECISIVE REASON THIS IS NOT 3 REMAINS: the issue's title question is not answered by its own supported candidate. open_questions[0] asks whether over-acceptance is a property of the MODELS or of the HARNESS, and neither source varies the decision threshold, the stated cost of a false positive, the availability of an explicit abstain option, or the presence of a human confirmation step. The issue text concedes that until that experiment is run, 'the models under-refuse' and 'these harnesses were built with no refusal affordance' are INDISTINGUISHABLE. The harness explanation is not hypothetical: src-0003 already established for a different sub-task that scaffolding can dominate measured reliability, and my G2 this cycle adds a third instance of measurement design dominating a headline number, since src-0005's 43-53% and 23-34% are all-or-nothing multiple-choice accuracies whose difficulty is set by the option sets, not by the underlying task alone. All five open_questions are unaddressed, including whether any precision-recall frontier exists (nobody has published the precision these models reach at a recall of 0.7, so it is unknown whether this is a tuning problem or a capability problem) and what the operational cost actually is (src-0007's ground truth IS the human analyst's accept/reject decision, so by construction it carries no human error bar and cannot say whether human triage would score better on its own benchmark). AN UNENTERED OBSERVATION THAT BEARS ON THE CENTRAL OPEN QUESTION, carried so it is not lost: src-0015's Table 1 has a Reward column no cycle has recorded (GPT-5.2 3.07, Sonnet 4.5 2.37, Gemini 3 2.61, DeepSeek 3.2 3.45), so THE MODEL THE PAPER CALLS BEST-CALIBRATED EARNS THE LOWEST REWARD and the two highest-containment models take the two highest rewards. That points at the harness rather than the models, which is precisely what open_questions[0] asks. Its caveats travel with it: the fetched material does not state the reward's composition, n = 40 per model with no CIs, and the association is not strictly monotone (DeepSeek outscores GPT-5.2 at lower containment). WHAT IS STILL ENTIRELY MISSING is the curl/HackerOne case -- the bug bounty ended 31 January 2026 after a flood of AI-generated reports, with roughly 20% of submissions AI slop by mid-2025 and the confirmed-vulnerability rate falling from about 15% to under 5%. It is currently an open_question on this issue and NOT evidence: no curl source exists in state/knowledge/index.json and G1 forbids inventing one. Cycles 19 and 22 judged it the highest-value uncollected source in the project and I agree; a T3 may add sources, so a T3 targeting this issue is the first realistic route to it. One pooling error to avoid, recorded at the candidate and repeated here: src-0015's 'calibration' is an action-threshold construct (false-positive rate, evidence-gating), NOT the ECE/Brier confidence calibration of src-0001 and src-0013, and the two must never be averaged or quoted as one measurement -- the same rule now also applies to src-0018's FDR/FNR abstention metrics. No open contradiction is filed against this issue, so no G3 adjustment applies.
